name: What is the difference between a garage conversion and a traditional home addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a garage conversion and a traditional home addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage conversion uses an existing roof, foundation, and exterior walls, which lowers overall construction complexity compared to building a home addition from the ground up. However, the tradeoff is losing covered vehicle parking, lawn equipment storage, or workshop space. A full home addition preserves your garage and allows you to expand the home’s exterior footprint, but it requires foundation excavation, concrete footings, new exterior framing, and extensive roof tie-ins. If your lot lacks setback space or you want to expand living space without expanding the home footprint, a garage conversion provides a practical alternative.
acceptedAnswer.description: A conversion reuses the existing structure and foundation to save time, whereas a home addition preserves your garage while building a brand-new exterior footprint.
